claims.claim: Reviewers report that the opening section and prologue are lengthy, taking multiple hours before free exploration begins.

citations.review_text:
A Huge Disappointment. Uninstalled After Just a Few Hours.
I had high expectations for Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, but the first few hours were so frustrating that I ended up uninstalling the game.

Here are my main complaints:

- An incredibly long and boring introduction. The opening story drags on endlessly, with excessive dialogue and sequences that constantly slow things down before you can even start exploring freely.

- An absurdly weak character at the beginning. Henry is practically defenseless. Almost any random passerby can kill you with ridiculous ease. I understand the intention to create a realistic progression system, but there's a huge difference between a challenging game and an unnecessarily frustrating one.

- A terrible combat system. The attack and defense mechanics are clunky, unintuitive, and frankly awful. Instead of making combat engaging and rewarding, they turn every encounter into an irritating experience.

- Completely inadequate tutorials. The game introduces countless mechanics without properly explaining them. The tutorials are extremely brief and largely useless, forcing players to constantly search the internet just to figure out how to perform even relatively simple tasks.

- Inexplicably limited crafting. For a game that prides itself on its historical realism and attention to detail, it's absurd that you can't even craft basic arrows for your bow. This makes absolutely no sense, especially when the game already includes elaborate blacksmithing and alchemy systems.

The fundamental problem is that this game constantly confuses realism with frustration. A game can be difficult and demanding while still being enjoyable and properly teaching players how its mechanics work.

After just a few hours, I realized I was spending more time fighting the controls and the game mechanics than actually having fun.

One of the most disappointing opening experiences I've had in a video game in years. Uninstalled without hesitation. Definitely no…

I played through the whole of KCD1 and enjoyed it. I thought the combat was a bit clunky but enjoyed the story so persevered. I tried KSC2 hoping they would improve the combat and it is just a bad as the first game. Crappy combat, waste of time small quests, boring dialogue. It is plainly just boring. The worst part is that the intro is over 3 hours long so you can't even get a feel for the game and return it on steam. Do not recommend.

It's kind of really slow in the beginning and very slow to get into the meat of it. I played 4 hours and just couldn't get into it which is frustrating because now I can't return it so here i am writing a review to warn people that unless you're unemployed or you've played the first one maybe there's no point even get this. My friend also tried to play this game and we both thought it would be good and fun but after putting 4 hours in, we haven't touched it in over 4months. 
Lastly, why on earth would i want to make potions the way that they did and why make the intro 4 hours long? not easy to get into the game and that's coming from someone who's played all the elder scrolls, chivalry, assassin creed, and any other applicable/relatable game.

# Great World, Terrible Combat System – A Frustrating Experience

I bought Kingdom Come: Deliverance II after seeing overwhelmingly positive reviews and hearing so much about its realistic medieval experience. Unfortunately, after several hours of playing, I am left feeling mostly frustrated and disappointed.

My biggest problem is the **combat system, which feels anything but realistic**.

Enemies seem capable of blocking almost every attack, instantly counterattacking, and unleashing endless combinations of strikes as if their stamina never runs out. Meanwhile, Henry quickly becomes exhausted after just a few attacks and blocks.

Even more ridiculous is the way enemies absorb damage. One opponent goes down after a few hits, while another, **wearing no helmet whatsoever, can take multiple sword strikes directly to the head and continue fighting as if nothing happened**. How exactly is that realistic?

Another major issue is the **terrible target-locking system and the lack of freedom of movement during combat**. When fighting two enemies, the camera practically glues itself to one opponent while the other freely attacks from the side. Simply backing away, switching targets, or controlling the distance becomes unnecessarily difficult and frustrating.

I am not asking for easy combat. I want combat that is challenging but also fair, logical, and consistent. Difficulty caused by an enemy's skill is one thing. Difficulty caused by clunky controls, restrictive movement, and poorly communicated mechanics is something entirely different.

On top of that, the game has an excessively long introduction, drawn-out conversations, a restrictive saving system, and unnecessarily inconvenient healing and recovery mechanics. Instead of enjoying exploration and character progression, I often feel like I am fighting against the game's own systems.

I am not saying the game has no strengths. The world is beautifully designed, detailed, and atmospheric, and the character progression sy…

This game is very visually appealing. That is where the compliments end, death by cutscene, awful combat controls, its a less fun, less whimsical skyrim. It wouldnt be terrible IF you didnt have to craft your ability to save the game.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the game provides vague hints and no directional markers for quests, forcing long periods of searching without guidance.

citation.review_text:
This game has no respect for your time. 

 if you have a busy schedule or are just looking to relax after a long day i would not recommend it. This game goes to the far end of no hand holding to the point of actively hindering you and preventing progress.

Ill give an example: I was tasked with finding a group of horse thieves. The NPC said the "the horse was tied to that sickly tree over there" with no pointing, direction, or marking in the middle of a forest of starved saplings and fallen trees.  So ive spent 30 minutes looking at random trees hoping for some kind of direction. You cant talk to the NPC again and the quest log adds nothing but "I have to track them down" there have been times when i have spent an hour on such tasks instead of getting an opportunity to enjoy the world or gameplay at the end of the day.

 Unless you have hours to spend figuring out hints that are made purposefully vague for the sake of an artificial difficulty spike this game isn't for you. The game is FILLED with moments like this. So im dropping the game. Hopefully the devs develop more respect for their players time in the future but for now, look elsewhere if you keep busy or just have stuff to do in general.

citations.review_text: combat ruins the game. it's chunky, and difficult to switch between opponents. looking around while engaged with one enemy almost isn't an option, and someone else can just come up and give you a free hit. almost impossible for new players to get past early battles without attempting 50 times because the stamina bar is outrageous - can only block 3-4 times in a row or attack 2-3 times, which isn't enough to even defeat a single enemy most times. story is done well, though, and they've certianly put some really good work into it. i have to say that it would be great if it had a proper combat system like Chivary II. i really like this game, and i'm thoroughly disappointed the combat has made it unplayable.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight minigames and non-combat activities like alchemy, blacksmithing, and smelting as enjoyable parts of the gameplay.

citations.review_text: Beautiful game with EXCEPTIONAL gameplay. Meaningfull progresion and the best part are the minigames for smelting and alchemy. Absolutely must play

I was such a fan of the first game that I grabbed this sequel completely blind, which ended up being the most regretful videogame purchase I think i've ever made in my life. 

This game strips away the most appealing aspects of the original, its historical accuracy and its likeable characters. Instead you will see insufferable immersion-breaking DEI inserts, charmless dull dialogue delivered reluctantly by voice actors who are capable of much more.

The gameplay is still just ok. Combat is still jank but a little more streamlined, the potionmaking and blacksmithing systems were good and even felt a little improved - I just wish they were in a different game.

It's overall a comfy RPG that you might get some value from if just want mindless combat or to do some virtual tourism. If you want a well crafted story or a charming RPG in a historical setting, this definitely isn't it.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a large open world with extensive side quests and exploration outside of the main campaign.

citations.review_text: One of the best games I've ever played. Really well optimized and runs smoothly. Did not finish the story yet but for now it is interesting and the characters are well written. There are a lot of side quests and activities outside of the main story. The open world looks realistic and is immersive.

I usually don't bother writing reviews, but this game... man.

I've played The Witcher and The Elder Scrolls, yet nothing quite captures the feeling of actually belonging in a world like Kingdom Come Deliverance.

I went straight into Hardcore mode on my first playthrough, and 73 hours in, i'm probably not even halfway through the story. Between side quests, scenic adventures, midnight stealth runs, treasure hunting, and the sheer amount of unexpected encounters that happen when you're simply trying to get from point a to b its just... my goodness.

This gentleman is the kind of game you don't rush. You slow down, take it all in, and savor every moment. Cause the atmosphere, the writing, the characters, the stories... everything just comes together beautifully.

Its one of the few games i've played where i can genuinely say it's worth every money spent.

This is the best game to come out since KCD1. The story is captivating and makes you look forward to the next time you get to play it. There are hours and hours of quests to keep you entertained. If you can get the DLC because after you get done with the base game you will be looking for something else to do and it's well worth it. Highly recommend this game

citations.review_text: This is such an amazing follow up to the first game. I think the initial skill curve can turn people away, but once you get the hang of it, this game is a treasure.

Hated it at first, now I love it
At first the combat drove me crazy. It felt clunky and pointless. But once I got the hang of it, everything clicked, and now the combat is one of the best parts of the game.

My only wish is a more interesting story, with the kind of twists and storylines The Witcher 3 has. Still, this is an awesome game. If the combat frustrates you early on, give it time. It’s worth it.

Recommended!

An amazing game, with so much love given to details. The world really felt alive and you can get a sense of real medieval day to day life.
The beginning was a bit hard to get used to, but after that it only got better.
Lengthy game, but well worth the time it takes to complete. Also gorgeous graphics and great gameplay. The beginning is pretty tough but just stick with it and it gets better!

Warhorse Studios you were expectionally brillant with your craftsmanship and effort with KCDII. I never thought another open-world RPG game would make me as addicted as i was, like with elder scrolls. Everything in this game was wonderful and I am so excited for KCDIII. If you havent played this game i would highly recommend playing this game but please give yourself 10-15hrs and the game will really pay off.

One of the most enjoyable First Person RPGs I've ever played. There is a steep learning curve when it comes to combat, but once you are past that hurdle, the gameplay and storyline is incredible. Highly recommended.

citations.review_text:
Normally, games like this let you be a tourist in their world, but Kingdome Come Deliverance 2 chose a different path: They made you an integral part of it. No other game has made me feel so immersed with its different systems and story. Even taught me a few things about medieval life.  One minor issue I have with are the sometimes occurring "press W and watch and don't play the videogame" segments.

So yeah, I don't know how to write reviews. Go get it, its great. 9/10

6.5/10 (Only recommended on SALE)

The world is genuinely beautiful. The attention to historical detail in the towns, the landscapes, the clothing, the day/night cycle... it’s impressive. Some characters are well-written, the voice acting is solid, and when the game stops getting in its own way it can create real atmosphere. (That’s the 6.5)

Everything else is the problem.

Combat is still the same clunky, stamina-draining, shield-bash rhythm game from the first one, only somehow more tedious. Fights drag on forever, if you play how the game tells you to. Perfect blocks and ripostes feel more like QTE timing than skill. The “realistic” combat is neither fun nor particularly realistic... it’s just slow and stubborn.

Stealth is a joke half the time. NPCs spin 180 degrees, do robotic moves like they’re on rails, detection is inconsistent, and yet the throwing stone is so overpowered that entire camps will happily follow it off a cliff. You can clear whole areas by yeeting rocks and stabbing people in the back, or just sit back with poisoned arrows while the AI panics and runs in circles.

There are long stretches where the game completely forgets it’s supposed to be a game and just tries to be a movie instead.  

You get locked into endless walk-and-talk sequences, auto-follow sections where your only real input is holding Alt and occasionally pressing the button to open the door the NPC just closed in your face, and long mandatory cutscenes (some of which even bug out and play with no dialogue audio). Your main activities are opening doors, listening to dialogue, and waiting for the next scripted moment. When I’m sitting at my desk with a mouse and keyboard I want to play, not sit through another five-minute muted Braveheart speech or follow a monk while the game holds my hand.

Endless progressive dialogue options that feel ripped out of 2020s Twitter while Henry still has to do a 2 minute long pray session for a perk avtivation. The writing loves to …

After finishing first game i just couldnt wait for to play continuation. It lived upto my expectation. Great story, quests, Very vast and rich world. You can enjoy game even without completing quest and for me it really felt like gta of medieveal time. This time they did great work on NPC, lores around world and environment. There is absolute zero progress on bugs still same as first game though people find fun in some bugs but still if you are at crucial point and if it causes your progress to fail or slow down its really disappointing. Also i think this isnt how henry and hans relationship should be turned out to be seeing from first game and start of this game. i thought he would start to consider henry as brother but its an option and can be avoided just surprising turn of thier relationship.
Now moving on to DLC
